title: Curcumin alleviates murine ulcerative colitis by modulating Tfh-B cell crosstalk via the CD40/CD40L costimulatory pathway.
authors: Yu, Ji; Liu, Yazhen; Huang, Jiaqi; Zhu, Xiyan; Liu, Duanyong; Zhao, Haimei; Deng, Bailing; Zhong, Youbao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究姜黄素通过CD40/CD40L通路调节Tfh-B细胞互作缓解溃疡性结肠炎，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心对象为蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联微弱。
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) progression is closely associated with dysregulated T follicular helper (Tfh)-B cell crosstalk, a process are centrally mediated through the CD40/CD40L costimulatory pathway. This study aimed to investigate whether curcumin (Cur) alleviates UC by regulating Tfh-B cell crosstalk via modulation of this pathway. Mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC were administered were treated with Cur for 14 consecutive days. Tfh and B cell subsets were analyzed using flow cytometry, while CD40/CD40L gene and protein expression were assessed via qRT-PCR and WB. Cellular spatial interactions were examined through immunofluorescence. Additionally, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate Cur's binding to the CD40/CD40L complex. Cur treatment significantly reduced the disease activity index, restored colon length, ameliorated histological damage, and suppressed proinflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-6, IL-21) as well as IgG levels. Mechanistically, Cur downregulated significantly CD40L(+) Tfh cells and CD40(+) B cells, and inhibited significantly key GC transcription factor Bcl-6 and plasma cell differentiation regulator Blimp-1. Molecular simulations confirmed that Cur stably binds to the CD40/CD40L interface through van der Waals forces and electrostatic complementarity, effectively blocking their interaction. The evidence from kinetic and competitive SPR assays demonstrates that Cur not only exhibits strong binding affinity by directly targeting CD40L, but also concentration-dependently blocks its interaction with CD40, resulting in significant functional inhibition of the CD40/CD40L signaling axis. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Cur ameliorates UC by inhibiting the CD40/CD40L complex, which disrupts pathological Tfh-B cell crosstalk and ultimately restores gut immune homeostasis.
abstract_zh: 溃疡性结肠炎（UC）的进展与滤泡辅助性T细胞（Tfh）-B细胞串扰失调密切相关，这一过程主要通过CD40/CD40L共刺激通路介导。本研究旨在探讨姜黄素（Cur）是否通过调节该通路调控Tfh-B细胞串扰从而缓解UC。采用葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的UC小鼠模型，连续14天给予Cur治疗。通过流式细胞术分析Tfh和B细胞亚群，利用qRT-PCR和WB评估CD40/CD40L基因和蛋白表达，并通过免疫荧光检测细胞空间相互作用。此外，进行了分子对接、分子动力学模拟和表面等离子体共振（SPR）以评估Cur与CD40/CD40L复合物的结合情况。Cur治疗显著降低了疾病活动指数，恢复结肠长度，改善组织学损伤，并抑制促炎细胞因子（如IL-6、IL-21）及IgG水平。机制上，Cur显著下调CD40L(+) Tfh细胞和CD40(+) B细胞，并显著抑制关键生发中心转录因子Bcl-6和浆细胞分化调节因子Blimp-1。分子模拟证实，Cur通过范德华力和静电互补性稳定结合于CD40/CD40L界面，有效阻断其相互作用。动力学和竞争性SPR实验证据表明，Cur不仅通过直接靶向CD40L表现出强结合亲和力，还以浓度依赖性方式阻断其与CD40的相互作用，导致CD40/CD40L信号轴显著功能抑制。综合这些发现表明，Cur通过抑制CD40/CD40L复合物缓解UC，从而破坏病理性Tfh-B细胞串扰，最终恢复肠道免疫稳态。
